key_insight: Training policies to optimize a vector of reward signals (rather than a single scalar) preserves behavioural diversity, which significantly improves performance when models are later used inside inference-time search procedures that select among many rollouts.
problem_solved: Standard post‑training that optimizes a single scalar reward collapses model outputs to low-entropy modes, reducing the variety of behaviors needed by search-based inference (e.g., AlphaEvolve) that relies on diverse candidate rollouts evaluated by different task-specific rewards.
method: Replace scalar-reward objectives with a vectorized reward optimization that treats multiple reward axes jointly, encouraging the model to represent a range of high-value behaviors.

Include diversity-preserving regularizers or objectives (e.g., entropy encouragement across reward dimensions or multi‑objective policy updates) so the trained policy yields varied rollouts at test time.
Integrate the vector-policy model into inference-time search pipelines to show that a richer candidate pool leads to better downstream selection under varied task-specific rewards.
impact: Practitioners can train models that retain useful behavioral diversity, making them more adaptable and robust when paired with search-based inference methods — reducing the need to retrain for every new reward during deployment.
visual_elements: Diagram comparing scalar-reward training (collapsing to one mode) vs vector-reward training (spread of behaviors across multiple axes).
Pipeline sketch showing: vector-policy training -> diverse rollouts -> inference-time search (selector) -> final output.
Heatmap or scatter plot illustrating coverage of reward space by rollouts from scalar-trained vs vector-trained models.

paper_title: Vector Policy Optimization: Training for Diversity Improves Test-Time Search
paper_authors: Ryan Bahlous-Boldi, Isha Puri, Idan Shenfeld, Akarsh Kumar, Mehul Damani
